title: HC Mike LaFleur Press Conference: November 6 | Week 9 vs. Seattle Seahawks
headline: Cardinals LT Jayden Williams and RB Bam Knight are out vs. Seattle. Josh Fryar steps in at left tackle, and Gardner Minshew is the QB after the Brissett trade.
summary: LaFleur opened by ruling out Bam Knight and Jayden Williams, and apparently Jon Gaines too, since the caption reads 'Gains'. He did not rule out a multi-week absence for Williams, the left tackle who left last week's game, but said he doesn't think so and will know more next week. Josh Fryar stepped in at left tackle so seamlessly that LaFleur didn't realize the swap had happened until about four plays later. Max Melton's recurring knee issue is unchanged, with the staff watching him through Sunday. Reporters also asked about Walter Nolen and Isaiah Adams (names garbled in the captions), and LaFleur said only 'we'll see on Sunday.' He called the Jacoby Brissett trade the best move for the organization and for Brissett, credited Minshew with giving the offense a spark, and said the offensive struggles were collective, starting with himself. He said Marvin Harrison Jr. and Brissett are no longer in the building, but the locker room is mature enough that it isn't a distraction. He is focused on a red zone plan, wants more explosive plays in the run game, and said Seattle's crowd noise will make communication hard, so he'll use wristbands and an early play call. He also praised a Seattle receiver and a versatile Seattle defender, and noted he has now faced Seattle five times in a calendar year.

title: Kevin Stefanski on Atlanta Falcons preparation for Cincinnati Bengals | Press Conference
headline: A player Stefanski called 'James' had his back flare up and was limited in the final Madrid practice. He is not on the roster, so the name is unclear, and Stefanski said more will be known in 24-48 hours.
summary: Stefanski spent most of the session on the Madrid trip, praising the hospitality and saying the team has handled travel and the changed routine well. The one injury item was a player the captions render as 'James Pierce', who is not on the roster. Stefanski said he had a good week and has held up his end of a very specific, structured process. A back issue flared up, he was limited in practice, and the team will know more in 24-48 hours. On the Bengals, he called them a powerful offense by air or ground, built around Joe Burrow, and said the goal is to slow them down rather than stop them. He said Bijan Robinson has a great mentality, will do whatever it takes to help the team win, and is focused solely on the team. He avoided any big-picture talk about eight games in, calling the season '17 sprints' and saying the focus is on this week. The team will walk through the Bernabéu the day before the game to check sightlines and the play clock. The bye comes after this game.

injuries.player: James (unidentified; name garbled in captions and not on roster)
injuries.detail: A back issue flared up and he was limited throughout the final practice. He had a good week before that. Stefanski said the team will know more in 24-48 hours.

signals.note: Stefanski responded to a question about Robinson's own comments on his level of play with strong praise of his mentality and no hint of any role change.

The team handled the travel, the hotel and the meetings well. A walkthrough at the Santiago Bernabéu is planned for the day before the game so players and quarterbacks can get used to the sightlines and the play clock.
Stefanski noted the unusual stretch of a weather-affected game last week, this game in Madrid, and the bye next week, and said the team will adjust to whatever the schedule is.
Stefanski said he doesn't track games played and treats the season as 17 sprints, with all focus on this week's challenge.

title: Jesse Minter: No Excuses, But the Result Is Not Acceptable
headline: Ravens are thin at QB after a 33-10 loss to Jacksonville. Minter wouldn't discuss Lamar Jackson's surgery or return, wouldn't confirm a Jacoby Brissett trade, and Kyle Hamilton left the game with an unknown injury.
summary: Minter said the Ravens got no excuses from him after the 33-10 Week 9 loss, their third straight defeat by 20 or more points. He pointed to an explosive play just before halftime that broke the game open, and said the team was aggressive there because the offense isn't built to come back by throwing all over the field. In the second half, he said, the Ravens got in their own way with back-to-back turnovers, while the defense spent nearly the whole half on the field. He called the pre-snap penalties unacceptable and said they are fixable, but that it will take new solutions such as different cadences or approaches. On the pass rush, he said one player is playing through having essentially one free hand, and that game situations have led opponents to run more conservative, run-heavy offenses. He wouldn't comment on a reported Brissett trade, but praised Joe (presumably Joe Fagnano) for playing on three days of prep while injured. He declined to discuss Lamar Jackson's surgery or a possible late-season return. He was noncommittal about Derrick Henry's wildcat snaps, calling them a response to that game's situation. He said he doesn't know much about Kyle Hamilton's injury yet and will have more information in the next day. He still believes the team has a path forward, though he admitted there is inconsistency in all three phases.

Minter says the team still has a path forward, citing spurts of good football in all three phases but a real lack of consistency, and says the team needs to find a formula that fits its current state.

title: Dave Canales gives final updates before Sunday's game against the Broncos
headline: Bryce Young (ankle) is ready to go after a phenomenal practice week, but Damien Lewis, Will Lee, Jaelan Phillips and Bobby Brown all missed every practice and are unlikely to play vs. Denver.
summary: Canales praised Friday's focus and energy. He said the O-line is still being sorted out, and that running back the same five from last week is possible. Lewis, Lee, Phillips and Brown did not practice all week and could not get on the field Friday. He said it would take something drastic for them to play, though he will check on them again Saturday. Bryce Young had some ankle soreness Monday, got checked out, and then practiced fully and looked great. Canales said he is ready to go. Tyrel Dodson was described as trusted and versatile and could start next to Devin Lloyd. At cornerback, Marco Wilson will play again, and practice-squad corners may compete for spots. He praised Denver's effort, discipline and pass rush, and called Bo Nix a winner who avoids turning bad plays into worse ones. Coaching staff changes were also discussed: Todd is energized in a new coordinator role, and a new hire was brought in. Canales said chemistry on the offensive line matters alongside having the best five.

title: Ben Johnson provides injury update for Week 9 vs. Buccaneers | Press Conference
headline: Kyle Monangai's toe injury is still lingering, and Theo Benedet (limited) and Grady Jarrett (rest and injury) are uncertain for the short-week Tampa Bay game.
summary: Ben Johnson said Chicago is on a short week before the Week 9 prime-time game against Tampa Bay, so it is hard to get a read on injured players. Theo Benedet went to the training room after Monday's game and was limited in practice, so today's session is the key test. Kyle's toe injury is getting better but has been fickle, and Johnson is hoping for a return each week without giving a timeline. Grady Jarrett sat out because of a mix of rest days and something he is feeling, and Johnson said he knows how big this game is. Johnson praised Rome Odunze's blocking mindset, calling it a big part of the offense, and said he likes rewarding blockers with the ball. He said Caleb Williams has grown most from year one to year two in relaying and communicating the game plan, apart from some snafus with crowd noise last week. He called the Bucs' Todd Bowles defense a tough run-stopping, single-high scheme with exotic pressure on passing downs. He also said fumbles (10 on the ground, 7 lost) are a concern he will study deeply during the bye.

title: Zac Taylor: "Our Guys Have Handled The Week Really Well" | PRESS CONFERENCE
headline: Shemar Stewart is in line for more defensive line snaps with Cashius Howell out, and Joe Burrow's offense is leading the NFL in passing yardage ahead of the Madrid game against Atlanta.
summary: Taylor spoke the Friday before Cincinnati's neutral-site game against the Falcons in Madrid. He said the team is acclimated after the travel, had a good practice Thursday, and spent Friday on the red zone. Injuries got only a vague answer: everybody is progressing and will be taken day to day, and Cedric Johnson was among the players asked about. He said Shemar Stewart will get a bigger opportunity because Cashius Howell is out, and that Stewart's slow start came from a deep D-line group and missed training camp, not from poor play. Taylor called Joe Burrow arguably the best passer in the world and said the offense will keep putting the ball in his hands, with the offensive line giving him time. He praised Dexter Lawrence's leadership and his late sack that forced overtime last week. He called Bryan Cook and Myles Murphy impactful leaders. He named the turnover battle, field position and red-zone touchdowns over field goals as the keys to the game. He noted the team leads the NFL in passing yards and is near the top in sacks, and said defensive penalties have improved recently.

title: Brian Schottenheimer on 105.3 The Fan | 11-06-26
headline: Caleb Downs and P.J. Locke are progressing, with Friday's practice the last hurdle. Jake Ferguson is only hoped to return to the field, and Joey Porter Jr. is still limited. Dallas expects Indianapolis to run through Jonathan Taylor.
summary: Schottenheimer opened by honoring Marshawn Kneeland on the one-year anniversary of his death and described the new Huddle 94 player-led mental health program. On the football side, he admitted the offense and run game were not good enough against Arizona (2.2 yards per carry) and put that on the coaching staff. He said the plan is to stay committed to the run by switching run types (inside zone, outside zone, misdirection) until a crease opens. He took responsibility as play caller for not closing out the Arizona game, saying only two field goals came in the second half. He said opponents' blitz pressure is the biggest difference this year and that Dallas hasn't yet 'gashed' it. He expects the Colts to blitz as well. On penalties, he singled out too many defensive offsides and Rashan Gary's roughing-the-passer penalty. On injuries, Caleb Downs and P.J. Locke need a full practice Friday, he hopes Jake Ferguson gets some work, and Joey Porter Jr. is expected to be limited but hopeful to play. For Indianapolis, he said the game will run through Jonathan Taylor, along with a quick-rhythm passing game built around Daniel Jones.

title: HC Sean Payton on Broncos’ WR corps: 'We have really good depth there'
headline: Pat Bryant (IR) is progressing and had a good week, while Payton praised WR depth of Troy Franklin, Marvin Mims Jr. and new addition Jaylen Waddle; no firm return date given.
summary: Payton described a normal Friday practice before the team travels. He credited drafting to strength and developing reserves for how well backups in the secondary have stepped in amid injuries, though he wouldn't say it's the deepest secondary he's had. He spoke about being named the team's Salute to Service nominee and his work with Canines for Warriors. On offense, he explained how trust with Bo Nix has grown, with Nix now anticipating his first short-yardage and red-zone calls. He discussed field position, using the rule that 100 yards of differential is worth about seven points, and said the new kickoff rule has changed how games start. Asked about Troy Franklin's increased snaps while Pat Bryant is on IR, he pointed to the receiver group's depth (Franklin, Marvin Mims Jr., and the trade for Waddle). On Bryant, he said the rookie has had a good week and is progressing, but gave no timeline.

signals.note: Named as part of the depth but no specific role was described, so his fantasy value stays tied to the rotation.

topics.detail: Reserve defensive backs have stepped up through injuries to starters. Payton credited drafting and development but wouldn't call it the deepest group he has had.

Payton said he and Nix are discussing which plays each likes, and that Nix now often knows the first short-yardage or red-zone call.

title: Campbell on injury updates
headline: Campbell doesn't expect D.J. Reed, Cade Mays or D.J. Wonnum to play Sunday, so Derrick Moore and other pass rushers get more work, while Alim McNeill is praised for interior pressure.
summary: Campbell opened by praising Alim McNeill's interior pass rush. title: Coen Reviews Win Over Ravens, Talks Team Culture & Approaching Trade Deadline | Press Conference
headline: TE Nate Boerkircher is on a roll with an explosive play in three straight games, and OL Wyatt Milum is a real part of the goal-line jumbo package.

He also said Boerkircher is good at the point of attack in the run game and is 'hitting a stride.' Coen wished the two had connected at the goal line on the fifth play of the game. He called the offense's second half 'missed opps.' He cited runs that could have been better and a third-down bubble throw against a blitz that likely would have been a touchdown. He was not concerned, since the game was in hand and he did not want to expose the quarterback and other starters. Coen described Wyatt Milum as a legitimate part of the jumbo package, with good hands and a place in the progression on a mesh concept. He also praised the defensive play-caller's energy, rapid-fire meeting style, and aggressive mix of fronts, coverages and pressures.

headline: Garrett Wilson is out vs. the Chiefs, Aaron Glenn says both Breece Hall and Braelon Allen will play, and David Bailey is back at full practice.
summary: Glenn opened with the injury report. Garrett Wilson is out, along with a player captioned as Trevin Wallace. A player captioned as "nation" sat out Friday with a back issue and is questionable. Joseph Ossai (limited) and Harrison Phillips (full) are both questionable. Breece Hall, Mason Taylor and David Bailey were full participants, and another player (captioned "Vijay") has just had his return window opened. Glenn said Wilson's absence is tough but that the team has other players to step up. On the backfield, he pushed back on the "who's the starter" framing and repeated that both backs will play. He called the offense's identity clear: run the ball, get Wilson the ball, and involve the other talented players. He praised the offensive line, especially Olu Fashanu's week-to-week improvement, and said the tight end room has multiple contributors with different traits. On defense he wants improvement on third-down penalties, passing-situation takeaways and interceptions, and he said Bailey has improved dramatically against the run. Kansas City is the opponent, with Mahomes, Kelce and Kenneth Walker as the main threats.

topics.detail: The offense has scored on its opening possession in four straight games. Glenn said each week starts with how to run the ball and how to get Garrett Wilson and the other talented players involved.

Glenn wants cleaner third-down play without penalties, continued run defense (about 2.9 yards per carry last week), and more takeaways in passing situations. He called the lack of interceptions surprising but pointed to forced fumbles as another way to take the ball away.

Glenn praised Kansas City's sustained success and Andy Reid's staff. He called Kenneth Walker a huge addition with contact balance and toughness, and said the Chiefs' run game is a big part of their offense. He said the Jets must squeeze the pocket against Mahomes.
Glenn said the line has played well in both run and pass, and that his preaching about the line's identity is paying off.
Glenn called it a great venue and said players tune out the atmosphere once the game starts.

title: Nick Sirianni Press Conference: November 6, 2026
headline: Eagles are starting QB Joe Milton against the Giants on Sunday and benching Tanner McKee. Sirianni was vague on whether McKee stays the backup, so Philly's passing game is a risk this week.
summary: Sirianni explained that he moved from Tanner McKee to Joe Milton at quarterback because he felt it gave the team the best chance to win this weekend. He praised McKee's play as solid and said the decision was not a punishment. He called the change fluid, saying his thinking developed as he looked at the game and built the game plan, even though he had backed McKee on Monday. He praised Milton's arm, athleticism, decision-making and confidence. Milton has been with the team about three weeks and has worked closely with the quarterback coaches to learn the offense. Sirianni mentioned that McKee escaped on a couple of scrambles and talked about mobility and the pass protection, but he stressed that injuries are not an excuse. He did not commit to McKee as the number two quarterback ('We'll see how that goes'). He said he expects McKee to handle the situation like a pro, as he did when Andy Dalton was briefly made the number two. He also defended keeping the news private for as long as possible, to protect the team and give the opponent less time to prepare. He said no coaching roles changed.

signals.claim: McKee will not start Sunday against the Giants; Joe Milton will start at QB.
signals.note: McKee loses the starting job despite the coach praising his play, which hurts the value of Eagles passing-game pieces tied to him.
signals.quote: I thought he did a lot of good things.

signals.claim: McKee's status as the number two quarterback is not confirmed.
signals.note: If Milton struggles, McKee could return to the starting role, but Sirianni did not commit to him as the backup.
signals.quote: We'll see how that goes.

topics.detail: Joe Milton, who joined about three weeks ago, gets the start over Tanner McKee. Sirianni cited his arm talent, athleticism, ability to process and confidence, and said the decision was made after discussion with the front office and offensive staff.

Sirianni acknowledged McKee escaped on a couple of scrambles during the last game and that part of the game matters. He said quarterbacks mostly need to play on time and in rhythm, and he did not use injuries as an excuse.
Word of the benching got out before Sirianni wanted it to. He said he holds information as long as possible to protect the team and limit opponent preparation. He said coaching roles did not change.

Sirianni said he has always believed in the quarterback room. He noted that McKee earned the backup job back after Andy Dalton was briefly made number two, and he expects McKee to respond the same way.

title: Head Coach Mike Macdonald Gives Final Updates Ahead Of Week 9 vs. Cardinals
headline: Seahawks are down to Drew Lock at QB with Darnold, Cross, Nelson, Shaheed, Leonard Williams and Nwosu all out. Nelson's knee procedure moves Bradford and Zabel back to guard.
summary: Macdonald opened by listing the players out for Week 9 against Arizona: Charles Cross, Sam Darnold, Quenton Nelson, Uchenna Nwosu, Brandon Pili, Rashid Shaheed and Leonard Williams. Connor O'Toole is questionable. Nelson will have a minor knee procedure and is week to week, but he won't go on IR because the timeline doesn't call for it. Macdonald said Nelson had the issue when he arrived and it was aggravated after re-imaging, and that he passed the physical. With Nelson out, Anthony Bradford goes back to right guard and Grey Zabel goes back to left guard. Macdonald said they chose those spots because the pair had banked reps there, and the decision came within the last 24 hours. Drew Lock starts despite an elbow the team has managed carefully this week, and Macdonald praised the quarterback work in practice. Leonard Williams and the other injured players simply did not improve enough to play, and no new IR talk was mentioned. Macdonald praised Bradford and Mike Morris for how they handled limited opportunities, and said Morris has earned his chance with Williams out. He was vague about restrictions on Zach and another player, saying only that there are parameters and that things are week to week.

title: Todd Bowles on Upcoming SNF Game vs. Chicago | Press Conference
headline: Tristan Wirfs is questionable for Sunday night's game vs. Chicago. He practiced and is progressing, and Bowles expects him to be okay.
summary: Bowles said left tackle Tristan Wirfs was out there giving it a go at Friday's practice. Wirfs made some progress the day before, and Bowles said he should be okay, though he is officially questionable and will be reassessed on Saturday for Sunday. A reporter asked whether one player was the only person Bowles would rule out, and Bowles said yes. The transcript doesn't make clear who that player is, so I haven't named anyone. Bowles credited special teams as a major factor in the last two wins through field position, turnovers, a blocked kick and made field goals in poor weather. He said Jalon Daniels has been helpful on the scout team imitating Caleb Williams, because he gives the defense a close look at a quarterback who can escape the pocket and run. Asked who would start in someone's place on Sunday, Bowles dodged, saying the reporter had already answered it. He also recalled playing at Soldier Field in a cold playoff win, which has no fantasy relevance.

signals.claim: Wirfs is trending toward playing Sunday vs. Chicago but remains questionable pending how he feels Saturday.
signals.note: Wirfs is a key pass protector for Baker Mayfield and the run game, so his status affects the whole offense, and his Saturday check-in is worth monitoring.
